description: Hourly rate excludes a shift with tips but no hours from BOTH sides of the division: shift A 10000c over 300 min plus shift B 10000c with nil hours, no rate policy, yields 2000c/h (not 4000) with coverage 1 of 2.
notes: Plan 'Metric registry' row hourlyRate: sum(earnedIncome over COVERED shifts) / sum(hours over COVERED shifts); nil without coverage; carries N of M. Plan Design 2 Queries: hourlyRateCents = coveredComponents.earnedIncomeCents * 60 / minutes, half-up, nil when minutes == 0; coveredComponents = sum over shifts WITH hours, knownComponents = sum over ALL shifts. No wage policy means regularWages = overtimeWages = 0 on every shift, so earnedIncome per shift = cash 10000 + credit 0 + gratuity 0 - tipOut 0 + 0 + 0 = 10000. Both shifts fall in the Mon-start workweek beginning 2026-09-28 (2026-09-28 is a Monday, 2026-09-29 a Tuesday; workweekStartWeekday 2). Arithmetic: covered set = {A} (only A has minutes). coveredEarnedIncome = 10000. minutes = 300. cumulative 300 <= threshold 2400 so regularMinutes 300, overtimeMinutes 0. hourlyRateCents = 10000 * 60 / 300 = 600000 / 300 = 2000 exactly (half-up (2*600000 + 300) / 600 = 1200300 / 600 = 2000 in integer division). Known set = {A, B}: knownEarnedIncome = 10000 + 10000 = 20000. Wrong answer 4000 = knownEarnedIncome 20000 * 60 / 300 = 1200000 / 300, i.e. putting B's tips in the numerator while B contributes no minutes to the denominator; the plan's PR 1 list names H1 as 'shift with tips and no hours excluded from both sides of $/hr'. Coverage reads 1 of 2 (coveredShifts / totalShifts); coverageSuffix pins the registry's 'N of M shifts' clause verbatim. asOf 2026-10-02 (a Friday) is after both work days so nothing is clamped out. Shift A: rates is empty, so Design 1 step 1 gives .rateNotSet and its 300 minutes still count toward the threshold (step 4). Shift B: wage is .unavailable; B has BOTH no rate policy (step 1 -> .rateNotSet) and nil minutes (step 4 -> .hoursMissing), and the plan states no precedence between the two reasons, so this fixture asserts only that B is unvalued and uncovered (the bare 'unavailable' form N3 also uses). The .rateNotSet-vs-.hoursMissing precedence is pinned by the dedicated Design 1 tests ('nil rate -> .rateNotSet with minutes counted; missing hours -> .hoursMissing'), not here. Completeness: only the four counts are asserted (totalShifts 2, shiftsWithHours 1, shiftsWageValued 0, shiftsWageAssumed 0). completeness.state and wageFeatureEnabled are intentionally NOT asserted: the plan (Design 2) lists .off and .partial(missingHours:missingRate:) but never defines how wageFeatureEnabled is derived or whether a dataset with no rate policy is .off or .partial with missingRate > 0 (the .partial caption '(or no rate set when that is the cause)' supports the second reading), the spec's H1 row asks nothing about completeness, and sibling N1 (also rate: []) reads the same situation as .partial(missingHours: 1, missingRate: 0). C1 owns completeness state. Reviewer correction: two reviewers cited docs/METRICS.md as resolving this ('.off (wage feature disabled or no rate policy)' / 'wageFeatureEnabled = rates.isEmpty'); neither string appears in docs/METRICS.md in this worktree (grep for 'disabled', 'isEmpty', 'wageFeatureEnabled' returns nothing), so the derivation is undefined everywhere and the removal stands on the plan alone. The registry's 'Averaging $X/hr' dollar format is not asserted: the plan does not pin '$20.00' versus '$20' (the app's only $/hr renderer today is Money.wholeDollarString, Payday/Utilities/Money.swift:19, fractionLength(0), which yields '$20/hr'), so the label's money half is a presentation decision for the main session, and coveredShifts/totalShifts plus coverageSuffix already pin the coverage fact the spec requires. The registry's nil-without-coverage rule for minutes == 0 is a different input set (every shift without hours) and is not asserted by H1; wrongAnswers holds only values the engine must NOT produce.
